data.title: Test & Certification Engineer
data.description:
About CynLr

Just like a baby's brain, CynLr Visual Intelligence stack makes Robots to instinctively see & pick any object under any ambience, without any training. (a demo video link). 

Today, a robot that can fit a screw into a nut without slipping a thread, doesn't exist. Imagine what it would take for a robot to assemble a Smartphone or a car by putting together 1000s of parts with varied shapes and weights, all in random orientations. Thus, factories become complex, needing heavy customization of their environment. 

CynLr-enabled visual robots intuitively learn to handle even unknown objects, on-the-fly, eliminating the need for rigid fixtures, pre-training, or environment customization. This enables an universal alternative to custom automation thus simplifying factory lines into modular LEGO-like micro-factories that can be rapidly reconfigured as products change. 

At the core of CynLr lies a fundamentally new approach to machine vision. Unlike conventional vision systems that rely on image recognition and heuristics, CynLr' s Vision and ML stacks are deeply inspired by neuroscience, modelling how biological vision understands shape, geometry, and interaction rather than appearance alone. To support this, CynLr builds its hardware, sensors, compute pipelines, and learning stacks from scratch, tightly coupling perception, decision-making, and action. 

This integration allows CynLr to operate in conditions that defeat traditional automation: variable lighting, cluttered environments, unknown objects, and high precision manipulation, unlocking automation use cases that have remained unsolved for decades. By rethinking vision as an intelligent, adaptive sense rather than a static tool, CynLr is redefining how robots perceive, reason, and interact with the physical world. 

About The Role

A robot that works in the lab is a prototype. A robot that can be sold, shipped and trusted around people is a certified product. The gap between the two is made of standards, test evidence and engineering discipline. 

CynLr's hardware spans an unusually wide range: the CLX dynamic stereo vision system with 400+ parts, the multi-arm CyRo robot, in-house robotic arms, high-power battery packs, and upcoming mobility platforms such as quadrupeds and AMRs. Each brings its own safety, EMC, battery and environmental requirements across India, EU/Switzerland and US markets. 

Certification cannot be an afterthought added at the end of design. It must shape architecture, component choices and test strategy from the first design review, so that every product reaches the market without costly redesigns. 

This role spans two broad scopes that work hand in hand. The first is Test Design: building the tests, rigs and evidence that prove our products work and are safe. The second is the Test & Certification Ecosystem: building the roadmaps, standards knowledge, and lab and regulator relationships that turn that evidence into certificates. Depending on your strengths, you may lead in one scope while contributing to the other. The Product Design, Battery & Power, and Mobility teams will be your internal customers. 

What You Will Do

Position 1 - Test Designer

- Designing DVT, PVT and end-of-line test plans derived from product requirements and standards
 - Designing and building test fixtures, automated test rigs and DAQ setups
 - Running pre-compliance tests for EMC, electrical safety and environmental stress (thermal, vibration, shock, IP)
 - Reliability testing (HALT/HASS, MTBF) and root-cause analysis of failures
 - Test rigs for battery packs and for mobile-robot safety (stability, stairs, slopes, collisions)Position 2 - Test & Certification Ecosystem: 

- Building certification roadmaps for each product and target market
 - Functional safety: risk assessments, safety requirement specifications, PL/SIL calculations, FMEA/FMEDA
 - Building and managing relationships with external labs and notified bodies (TÜV, UL, Intertek, etc. )
 - Tracking regulatory changes across India, EU/Switzerland and US
 - Owning technical files, Declarations of Conformity and certification submissionsShared by both positions: 

- Embedding compliance and testability into design from day one
 - Maintaining full traceability from requirement to test to certificate
 - Acting as the test and compliance knowledge base for design engineers across the organization

What Are We Looking For

Common to both positions

- 5-8 years in product test, certification or compliance for industrial automation, robotics, automotive, EV or similar electromechanical products. 
 - Clear technical writing for test reports, risk assessments and technical files. 
 - Working exposure to all of these standards areas: 
 - Robots and machinery: ISO 10218-1/-2, ISO/TS 15066, EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, IEC 60204-1, ANSI/A3 R15. 06, UL 1740
 - Functional safety: ISO 13849-1/-2, IEC 62061, IEC 61508
 - Mobile robots: ISO 3691-4, ANSI/A3 R15. 08, UL 3100
 - EMC and radio: IEC 61000-6-2/-4, CISPR 11, EU RED, FCC Part 15, India WPC/TEC
 - Batteries: IEC 62133-2, IEC 62619, UL 2271, UN 38. 3, BIS IS 16046, EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542
 - Environmental: IEC 60068, IEC 60529Position 1 - Test Designer: 

- Hands-on with oscilloscopes, power analysers, EMC pre-scan equipment and DAQ systems. 
 - Experience designing test fixtures and rigs, including basic mechanical and electrical design. 
 - Test automation in Python, LabVIEW or equivalent. 
 - Strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills. Position 2 - Test & Certification Ecosystem: 

- At least one product taken through CE, UL or equivalent certification end to end. 
 - Experience with functional safety analysis and documentation. 
 - Experience working with test labs, notified bodies and regulators, and managing certification timelines and costs. Good to Have: 

- TÜV Functional Safety Engineer certification or equivalent. 
 - Experience certifying battery packs or mobile robots. 
 - Exposure to vision or optical system testing. 

Team Structure & Growth

As mentioned earlier, this role spans two broad scopes that work hand in hand. The first is Test Design: building the tests, rigs and evidence that prove our products work and are safe. The second is the Test & Certification Ecosystem: building the roadmaps, standards knowledge, and lab and regulator relationships that turn that evidence into certificates. Depending on your strengths, you may lead in one scope while contributing to the other. The Product Design, Battery & Power, and Mobility teams will be your internal customers. 

Beyond specializing in the role of Test & Certification Engineers, this position offers growth into test, compliance and quality leadership roles as the organization scales. The Test Designer can grow into test architecture, test automation and reliability engineering; the Ecosystem engineer into functional safety, product compliance management and regulatory strategy. 

The role can also evolve into cross-functional and customer-facing opportunities such as supplier quality, customer audits, regulatory strategy for new markets and solution engineering, based on individual interests and business needs.

data.title: < ASIC > Physical Design Engineer
data.description:
Role: Senior ASIC PD Engineer

Own the end-to-end RTL-to-GDSII implementation for complex IP/SoC subsystems and build the backend team that scales it. You'll define the methodology, constraints, and quality metrics that the team shall adhere to. The team you lead will be responsible for synthesis, floor planning, P&R, clock tree synthesis, multi-corner STA, design for testability, and ECOs to achieve sign-off. You and your team will collaborate tightly not only with our RTL/digital team but also with our full-custom and full-custom layout team, integrating our full-custom design blocks into a digital-on-top mixed ASIC design. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, where you will not only set the flow and lead the team, but also personally de-risk and own the most challenging aspects of the design. 

What you'll do

- Methodology: Define and maintain a modern RTL-to-GDS flow, including constraint strategy, libraries/PDKs, UPF/CPF, and sign-off checks. 
 - Implementation: Run synthesis, floorplan, partitioning, P&R, CTS, routing, extraction, and closure.   
 - PPA & quality: Create predictable PPA targets and tracking, lead timing/power ECOs; correlate pre/post-layout timing
 - Integration: Integrate custom macros, SRAMs, and I/O, manage clocking strategy, CDC, and hierarchical/hard-macro integration with LEF. 
 - Low power: Own power intent (UPF/CPF), isolation/retention strategies, level shifting, and power-aware STA/simulation. 
 - DFT & test hooks: Partner with DFT on scan/MBIST insertion and test timing; ensure routes and constraints don't compromise test coverage or bring-up. 
 - Automation & CI: Industrialize the flow with Tcl/Python automation, reproducible configurations, metrics dashboards, and CI/CD for nightly builds and regression testing. 
 - Foundry interface: Engage with foundries on PDK updates, waiver handling, antenna/density rules, and reliability guidance; maintain the flow of information. 

Requirements

- Deep expertise in one complete tool chain (Synopsys or Cadence)
 - Hands-on experience in power-optimization techniques, including glitch reduction and activity-based power correlation (VCD/SAIF). 
 - Strong MCMM STA and timing-closure experience
 - Experience with grid planning, IR/EM analysis, and fixes. Proven floorplanning/partitioning and hierarchical integration (hard-macros, abstracts/LEF, feedthroughs, blockage strategy). 
 - UPF/CPF know-how for multi-voltage, power-gated designs, including isolation/retention and power-aware STA and sim. 
 - Scripting for automation (Tcl, Python) and version control (Git, Perforce, or similar)
 - Ability to work and lead the activities independently and assume responsibility for major decisions

Nice to have

- DFT exposure (scan planning, test timing, MBIST integration) and formal equivalence workflows. 
 - Package/board co-design awareness (bump/rail planning, SSO/PI, thermal assumptions). 
 - Experience at advanced nodes (≤ 7 nm FinFET) with multi-patterning/EUV constraints and variability considerations. 
 - Familiarity with sign-off for safety-/quality-critical markets (automotive-style reliability targets, waiver governance, documentation rigor).

data.title: Technology Controls Testing Manager
data.description:
A global, digitally enabled business that empowers a brighter future by connecting millions of people with their assets - safely, securely and responsibly. Through our two businesses MUFG Retirement Solutions and MUFG Corporate Markets, we partner with a diversified portfolio of global clients to provide robust, efficient and scalable services, purpose-built solutions and modern technology platforms that deliver world class outcomes and experiences. A member of MUFG, a global financial group, we help manage regulatory complexity, improve data management and connect people with their assets, through exceptional user experience that leverages the expertise of our people combined with scalable technology, digital connectivity and data insights. 

Overview

As an experienced Technology controls & assurance professional, you will lead the Technology Controls Function, overseeing controls documentation, controls testing and control effectiveness activities across Technology. 
The role is accountable for the operation, quality and continuous improvement of the Technology Controls Testing Regime, ensuring Technology controls are appropriately documented, consistently tested and aligned to regulatory, risk and business expectations. Working closely with Technology leadership, control owners, Risk stakeholders, Audit Delivery and Line 2 assurance providers, the role provides a single point of accountability for controls testing outcomes and associated governance activities. 
Leading a team comprising the Documentation & Controls Analyst and Controls Testers, you will establish consistent methodologies, quality standards and reporting practices that improve control maturity, strengthen governance outcomes and provide meaningful insight into the effectiveness of the Technology control environment. 
The role contributes to a proactive and sustainable controls capability by identifying recurring weaknesses, emerging risks and opportunities to strengthen governance, operational resilience and assurance outcomes across Technology. The role supports audit and regulatory activities by providing reliable controls documentation, testing outcomes and remediation validation results, while accountability for audit delivery and audit readiness remains with the Audit Delivery function. 
Key Accountabilities and main responsibilities
Strategic Focus  

- Lead the ongoing development and maturity of the Technology Controls Function, supporting a risk-based and repeatable approach to controls documentation and controls testing. 
 - Establish and maintain consistent methodologies, standards and quality frameworks across controls testing and documentation activities. 
 - Drive improvements in control maturity by identifying recurring control weaknesses, emerging risks and opportunities for uplift across the Technology control environment. 
 - Support regulatory compliance and assurance obligations through ongoing oversight of Technology controls across key risk domains. 
 - Promote a culture of proactive control management, continuous improvement and evidence-based decision-making across Technology. 
Operational Management  

- Develop and maintain annual and quarterly controls testing plans, ensuring coverage aligns with Technology risks, regulatory obligations, material changes and assurance requirements. 
 - Manage and oversee the activities of the Documentation & Controls Analyst and Controls Testers, ensuring delivery priorities align with Technology risk, control and governance objectives. 
 - Oversee the execution of design effectiveness and operating effectiveness testing, ensuring testing is completed consistently and in accordance with approved methodologies. 
 - Review control assessments, testing workpapers, identified exceptions and supporting evidence to ensure conclusions are accurate, evidence-based and defensible. 
 - Oversee remediation validation activities and ensure validation conclusions appropriately address the identified control deficiency and agreed corrective actions. 
 - Oversee the maintenance of the Technology control inventory and ensure control documentation remains current, complete and aligned with testing requirements. 
 - Ensure effective coordination between control documentation, evidence management, control owner engagement and controls testing activities. 
 - Provide controls testing outcomes, control effectiveness assessments, documentation insights and remediation validation results to support audit, regulatory and assurance activities across frameworks including GS007, J-SOX, CPS 230 and CPS 234. 
People Leadership  

- Lead, coach and develop the Documentation & Controls Analyst and Controls Testers, providing clear direction, technical guidance and quality oversight. 
 - Establish work priorities, delivery expectations and quality standards across the Technology Controls Function. 
 - Allocate and monitor activities across controls documentation and controls testing, ensuring appropriate coverage and timely delivery of agreed outcomes. 
 - Build effective working relationships with Technology leadership, control owners, service owners, Technology SMEs, Risk stakeholders, Audit Delivery and assurance providers. 
 - Provide constructive challenge where control design, control operation, documentation, evidence quality or remediation activities do not meet required standards. 
 - Support capability uplift across Technology by improving stakeholder understanding of control ownership, control effectiveness, documentation expectations and testing requirements. 
 - Foster collaboration between controls testing, documentation, audit delivery and risk functions while maintaining clear accountability for their respective activities. 
Governance & Risk

- Ensure controls documentation, controls testing and supporting evidence remain aligned, complete, traceable and defensible. 
 - Provide management reporting and governance insights on control effectiveness, testing outcomes, recurring weaknesses, remediation progress and emerging risks. 
 - Monitor themes across control testing results, documentation reviews, audit findings and remediation activities to identify systemic control concerns and improvement opportunities. 
 - Escalate material control weaknesses, repeated exceptions, overdue actions and significant risk exposures through appropriate management and governance channels. 
 - Ensure controls testing activities are performed objectively and consistently in accordance with approved methodologies, governance requirements and quality standards. 
 - Maintain appropriate separation between control ownership, control operation, documentation support, controls testing and independent assurance activities. 
 - Support continuous improvement of Technology governance and assurance practices through measurement, thematic analysis and practical recommendations for strengthening control effectiveness. 
The above list of key accountabilities is not an exhaustive list and may change from time-to-time based on business needs. 
Experience & Personal Attributes
Experience  

- 5-7 years' experience in Technology Risk, IT Audit, Controls Assurance, Technology Governance, Compliance or related assurance functions. 
 - Demonstrated experience leading or managing Technology controls testing, assurance, audit or risk programs within a complex Technology environment. 
 - Strong experience assessing the design and operating effectiveness of Technology controls, including walkthroughs, sampling, evidence evaluation, exception assessment and remediation validation. 
 - Strong working knowledge of Technology control domains including (but not limited to) Identity & Access Management, Privileged Access Management, Change Management, Backup & Recovery, Resilience, Asset Management and Third-Party Risk. 
 - Experience developing and implementing controls testing methodologies, testing plans, sampling approaches, quality assurance processes and governance practices. 
 - Experience overseeing or managing teams responsible for controls documentation, controls testing, Technology assurance, governance or risk activities. 
 - Strong understanding of regulatory and assurance frameworks including (but not limited to) GS007, J-SOX, CPS 234, ISO 27001, or similar control environments. 
 - Experience producing management reporting, governance insights and thematic analysis for senior leadership and governance forums. 
 - Experience engaging with senior Technology stakeholders, control owners, external auditors, Risk and Compliance functions and other assurance providers. 
 - Experience within financial services or another highly regulated industry is highly desirable. 
Personal Attributes

- Strong leadership capability, with the ability to set clear expectations, develop team capability and drive accountability for quality outcomes. 
 - Highly analytical and able to identify systemic control weaknesses, recurring themes and emerging risks across a complex Technology environment. 
 - Strong judgement and decision-making skills, with the ability to balance risk, control effectiveness and practical business outcomes. 
 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex control and assurance matters to technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 - Confident stakeholder engagement style, with the ability to provide constructive challenge while maintaining effective working relationships. 
 - Strong attention to detail combined with the ability to understand broader risk, governance and organisational implications. 
 - Results-oriented approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes within agreed timelines. 
 - Collaborative leadership style focused on coaching, knowledge sharing and developing sustainable team capability. 
 - Demonstrates integrity, professionalism and objectivity, with a commitment to evidence-based and defensible assurance outcomes. 
 - Continuous improvement mindset, with a focus on strengthening control maturity, documentation quality, testing effectiveness and governance outcomes.

We are looking for an experienced Engineering Lead to take end-to-end technical ownership of a critical Grid & Devices domain within an innovative energy technology platform. data.title: Sr Software Engineer - Coding Agents
data.description:
Lexsi  Labs  is  the  leading  frontier  AI  lab  focused  on  building  aligned,   interpretable,   and  safe  superintelligent  systems.   While  that  is  the  vision,   the  mission  to  build  safety  aware  autonomous  system  in  the  extreme  near  term.   Our  research  work  spans  around  areas  like  AI  alignment  methodologies,   interpretability led  system  design,   and  foundational  model  research  across  structured,   tabular,   and  new  autonomous  system  designs.   We  published  about  25+  papers  in  the  past  15  months  across  leading  conferences  ICLR,   ICML,   WWW,   IJCNN,   MICCAI,   Eurips  etc.   Our  labs  are  located  in  India  (Mumbai  &  remote),   Paris,   &  London.   

We  operate  with  a  flat  structure,   high  autonomy,   and  a  strong  bias  toward  engineers  who  take  full  ownership  of  what  they  build,   from  architecture  to  production  behavior. 

The  Role

Our  current  sprint  on  building  autonomous  system  for  complex  problems,   across  software  engineering,   data  science,   and  AI  research  involves  building  harness,   execution  substrate  and  evaluation  system,   and  each  is  designed  to  run  inside  a  customer's  environment  rather  than  ours. 

This  role  owns  the  coding  agent:   a  system  that  takes  an  objective,   works  directly  on  a  repository,   verifies  its  own  changes,   and  produces  a  record  of  what  it  did.   The  codebases  are  large,   old,   thinly  tested  and  load-bearing,   and  the  agent  runs  inside  the  customer's  network,   usually  without  internet  egress. 

What'll  you  work  on:   

- The  agent  architecture  and  its  tool  surface  for  software  work,   including  retrieval,   editing,   builds,   tests,   static  analysis  and  version  control. 
 - Verification,   so  that  a  change  is  established  as  correct  before  a  human  sees  it. 
 - Long-horizon  execution  across  multi-file  refactors  and  migrations,   with  checkpointing,   recovery  and  self-correction. 
 - The  authorisation  and  rollback  model  governing  what  the  agent  may  do  and  how  it  is  undone. 
 - Integrations  with  the  engineering  estate  the  agent  operates  in,   and  the  observability  tooling  used  to  debug  and  audit  it. 
 - Evaluation  suites  built  from  real  repository  tasks,   and  the  behavior  tuning  that  follows  from  them. 

You  will  work  closely  with  our  research  team  on  evaluation  design,   post-training  and  interpretability  of  agent  behavior. 

What  We  Are  Looking  For

This  is  a  developer  tooling  role  as  much  as  an  AI  role.   The  agent  is  only  as  capable  as  the  tools  and  integrations  it  is  given,   so  depth  here  matters  more  to  us  than  anything  else. 

- Deep  experience  with  developer  tooling  and  IDEs.   Editor  and  IDE  internals  or  extensions,   language  servers  and  LSP,   code  intelligence,   refactoring  engines.   You  have  built  things  engineers  use  every  day. 
 - Code  intelligence  and  program  analysis.   ASTs  and  tree-sitter,   static  and  dataflow  analysis,   symbol  indexing  and  code  search,   call  graph  and  dependency  resolution,   codemods  and  automated  migration  tooling. 
 - Build  systems  and  CI/CD.   Bazel,   Gradle,   Maven,   Make  and  similar,   incremental  and  hermetic  builds,   artifact  and  dependency  management,   pipeline  design  across  Jenkins,   GitLab,   GitHub  Actions  or  equivalents,   including  self-hosted  and  offline  deployments. 
 - Observability.   Distributed  tracing,   structured  logging,   OpenTelemetry,   and  building  the  replay  and  inspection  tooling  that  makes  non-deterministic  systems  debuggable. 
 - Integrations  engineering.   Git  hosting  APIs,   ticketing  and  workflow  systems,   enterprise  auth,   and  the  reality  of  working  against  self-hosted  software  several  versions  behind  current. 
 - Agentic  systems  in  production,   not  prototypes.   You  know  the  current  framework  landscape  (ReAct-style  agents,   LangGraph,   LangChain,   Semantic  Kernel)  and  where  each  one  stops  working. 
 - Strong  backend  fundamentals.   Advanced  Python,   APIs  and  services,   sandboxing  and  containerisation,   databases  and  data  pipelines,   cloud  and  on-premise  infrastructure. 
 - You  reason  about  performance,   reliability,   cost,   safety  and  interpretability  as  one  connected  set  of  constraints. 
 - You  make  good  calls  in  the  gray  area,   and  you  are  comfortable  when  problems  are  loosely  specified  and  ownership  is  assumed  rather  than  assigned. 
 - Experience  building  evaluation  datasets  or  frameworks  for  AI  systems  is  a  plus. 
 - Compiler  background,   large  monorepo  work,   or  legacy  modernisation  programs  are  a  plus. 
 - Prior  exposure  to  alignment,   interpretability  or  safety  tooling  in  production  settings  is  a  plus. 

We  move  quickly  and  expect  candidates  to  do  the  same.   We  value  substance  over  polish  and  execution  over  rhetoric.

data.title: Staff / Principal Defensive Security Engineer (Frontier Cyber Models)
data.description:
Hiring for Lean SuperIntelligence - via Flexiple, the recruiting partner on this role. 

About the Company

LSI (Lean SuperIntelligence) is a security AI lab building self-improving cybersecurity LLMs. LSI-Offense-1 finds, exploits and validates vulnerabilities; LSI-Defense-1 detects, investigates and responds to attacks. The two train against each other inside LSI Cyber World Models, realistic instrumented enterprise environments where every outcome is verified, and they run on-prem or air-gapped inside the enterprise that owns them. 

LSI is founded by the team behind India's first sovereign LLM and AI labs at Alexa, Uber AI and Salesforce Research, with elite security researchers, and is backed by Accel, Fusion Fund, SVQ, Inventus Capital and Dreamit Ventures, plus angels who led AI and security at OpenAI, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne and Zscaler. 

About the Role

You are the defender in LSI's self-play loop. You will turn what the best detection engineers, threat hunters, malware analysts and incident responders do into the environments, data, rewards and evaluations that make LSI's defense model detect, correlate, investigate and triage real attacks with fewer false alarms. 

You will also architect how the model plugs into a real SOC: the telemetry it reads, the correlations it draws, the evidence it shows and the actions it is trusted to take. Level (Staff or Principal) is set by scope and track record. 

What you'll do

- Set the technical direction and evaluation strategy for detection, alert triage, correlation, investigation and response recommendations. 
 - Build instrumented environments that produce realistic telemetry (EDR, cloud audit, identity, network, Kubernetes, SaaS, AI-agent traces) with ground-truth labels from offense-team attacks. 
 - Encode the analyst: turn detection engineering, hunting and IR tradecraft into tools, investigation playbooks, expert trajectories and reward functions. 
 - Design how the model links weak signals across sources and time into an attack story mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and the asset and identity graph. 
 - Build pipelines where the model drafts, tests and tunes detections (Sigma, KQL, SPL, ES|QL, YARA) against replayed attacks, and extend defensive benchmarks (ExCyTIn-Bench, DiagChain-style, triage precision/recall). 
 - Architect SOC integration with SIEM, XDR and SOAR (Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel, Chronicle, CrowdStrike, Cortex) and run design-partner pilots. 

What you bring

- 5+ years of hands-on defense (8+ for Principal) across at least three of: detection engineering, threat hunting, incident response and forensics, SOC architecture, threat research and intelligence, malware analysis. 
 - Has built detection programs, not just rules: detection-as-code pipelines, coverage models and tuning loops at an enterprise, cloud provider, MDR or security vendor. 
 - Has led investigations against sophisticated adversaries across endpoint, cloud, identity and network. 
 - Strong with query languages and large-scale log pipelines; understands entity resolution, timelines, baselining and why correlations fail. 
 - Has built or extended LLM-driven triage, investigation, hunting or detection-authoring workflows with measured results. 
 - Fluent in Python plus one of Go, Rust or TypeScript; comfortable with Kubernetes, IaC and streaming data. 

Nice to have

- RL environments, simulators, reward functions or verifiers; post-training for agentic tasks. 
 - Hands-on malware reverse engineering (Ghidra, IDA, sandboxes) and original research that shipped detections. 
 - Built agentic SOC or autonomous investigation features at a security vendor or AI lab. 
 - Detection and response for AI systems (OWASP LLM / Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS). 
 - Open-source detection content, publications or talks at Black Hat, DEF CON, SANS, FIRST or similar.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal Cloud Platform Engineer based in India. 

We are seeking an accomplished and hands-on Principal Cloud Platform Engineer to shape the architecture, reliability, and evolution of a large-scale cloud infrastructure environment. In this senior technical leadership role, you will drive the long-term platform strategy across AWS and Google Cloud while remaining actively involved in software development and production operations. You will design and build scalable infrastructure services, internal developer platforms, and automation solutions that empower engineering teams to deliver software securely and efficiently. You will also take ownership of multi-region architecture, Kubernetes environments, infrastructure reliability, and disaster recovery capabilities. Working across distributed engineering teams, you will establish technical standards, resolve complex production challenges, and mentor senior engineers. This is an opportunity to influence critical cloud infrastructure supporting a global SaaS platform while driving innovation, operational excellence, and AI-assisted engineering practices. 

Accountabilities

- Cloud Platform Architecture & Technical Strategy
 - Define and lead the long-term technical direction and multi-year architecture strategy for cloud platforms across AWS and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). 
 - Own architectural decisions covering compute, networking, Kubernetes, databases, data stores, and edge infrastructure. 
 - Design scalable, secure, resilient, and cost-efficient cloud environments supporting globally distributed services. 
 - Establish architectural standards and technical best practices across multiple engineering teams. 
 - Lead infrastructure modernization initiatives and ensure platform architecture evolves alongside business and product requirements. 
 - Software Engineering & Platform Development
 - Design, develop, and maintain production-grade platform services and automation using Go, Python, or other relevant programming languages. 
 - Build Kubernetes controllers, operators, internal APIs, command-line interfaces (CLIs), and tools that simplify infrastructure management. 
 - Develop and continuously improve internal developer platforms, including self-service provisioning, standardized deployment workflows, and reusable engineering solutions. 
 - Implement and maintain CI/CD and GitOps pipelines, particularly using Argo CD, to improve deployment reliability and engineering productivity. 
 - Reduce manual operational work through automation and developer-focused tooling. 
 - Reliability, Scalability & Production Operations
 - Design and maintain multi-region cloud architectures, automated failover mechanisms, and disaster recovery strategies. 
 - Define and test Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) to ensure business continuity. 
 - Participate in on-call rotations and act as a senior technical escalation point during critical production incidents. 
 - Lead incident response activities and translate findings from blameless post-incident reviews into permanent engineering improvements. 
 - Establish and maintain service reliability standards, including Service Level Indicators (SLIs), Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, production readiness reviews, and capacity planning. 
 - Maintain platform availability targets of 99. 99% while supporting continued infrastructure growth. 
 - Identify and resolve performance and scalability bottlenecks across applications, databases, queues, and network infrastructure. 
 - Infrastructure, Networking & Security
 - Lead edge and traffic engineering initiatives involving ingress management, load balancing, DNS, content delivery networks (CDNs), web application firewalls (WAFs), and service mesh technologies. 
 - Own Infrastructure as Code (IaC) architecture using Terraform across multi-account and multi-region cloud environments. 
 - Establish reusable Terraform modules, effective state management practices, and policy-as-code controls. 
 - Ensure infrastructure meets security, compliance, availability, and operational requirements. 
 - Implement and improve cloud networking, access management, and infrastructure security practices. 
 - Cost Optimization & AI-Enabled Engineering
 - Partner with FinOps and engineering teams to optimize cloud spending through resource right-sizing, cost monitoring, and improved infrastructure utilization. 
 - Incorporate infrastructure costs and unit economics into architectural decisions. 
 - Introduce AI-assisted engineering tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot, to improve development productivity, tooling, documentation, and incident investigation. 
 - Identify opportunities to leverage automation and AI to simplify platform operations and improve engineering efficiency. 
 - Technical Leadership & Mentorship
 - Produce technical RFCs, architecture documentation, and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) to communicate and formalize engineering decisions. 
 - Review architecture and technical designs across engineering teams, ensuring consistency and high-quality implementation. 
 - Mentor senior and staff engineers, helping strengthen technical capabilities and engineering standards. 
 - Influence technical direction across multiple teams without relying on direct reporting authority. 
 - Promote knowledge sharing, collaboration, and continuous improvement throughout the engineering organization. 
Requirements

- At least 12 years of professional software engineering experience, including a minimum of 5 years in Platform Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), or DevOps roles supporting large-scale, business-critical SaaS environments. 
 - Strong hands-on software development experience, with a proven track record of designing, building, testing, and deploying production services using Go, Python, or Java. 
 - Deep understanding of distributed systems, API design, concurrency, software testing, and large-scale system architecture. 
 - Extensive practical experience operating business-critical, 24/7 production systems, including on-call responsibilities, incident management, and troubleshooting across application, operating system, networking, and cloud infrastructure layers. 
 - Advanced expertise in AWS cloud services, particularly IAM, VPC architecture, Transit Gateway, Application and Network Load Balancers (ALB/NLB), Route 53, EKS, and managed data services. 
 - Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is an advantage. 
 - Strong production experience with Kubernetes at scale, including cluster lifecycle management, networking, autoscaling, RBAC, controllers, operators, and GitOps workflows using Argo CD. 
 - Advanced proficiency in Terraform, including module architecture, state management, infrastructure refactoring, and multi-account deployment patterns. 
 - Hands-on experience with observability and monitoring platforms such as Datadog, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry. 
 - Proven ability to define and improve reliability metrics, service-level objectives, and incident management processes, with measurable improvements in Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR). 
 - Demonstrated principal-level technical leadership, including setting architectural direction across multiple teams, influencing engineering decisions, and successfully leading complex migrations. 
 - Strong technical documentation and communication skills, with the ability to explain architectural decisions and trade-offs involving cost, risk, scalability, and delivery timelines to both engineers and senior leadership. 
 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 
 - Excellent collaboration, problem-solving, and mentoring skills, with the ability to work effectively in distributed engineering environments. 
 - A proactive mindset aligned with continuous improvement, technical innovation, building strong professional relationships, and delivering measurable engineering outcomes. 
 - Willingness and ability to participate in scheduled on-call rotations and respond to critical production alerts during assigned shifts. 
 - Fluency in written and spoken English, as it is the primary language used for international collaboration and recruitment. 

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience building internal developer platforms, developer portals, or self-service infrastructure solutions using Backstage or comparable technologies. 
 - Practical knowledge of service mesh technologies such as Istio or Linkerd. 
 - Experience with proxies and traffic management tools, including Envoy, HAProxy, and NGINX. 
 - Familiarity with CDN architecture, WAF solutions, and DDoS protection strategies. 
 - Experience scaling data platforms and services such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, or Kafka, including multi-region and active-active architectures. 
 - Knowledge of chaos engineering practices and experience organizing regular resilience testing or game days in staging and production environments. 
 - Strong security engineering background, including secrets management solutions such as HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and External Secrets Operator. 
 - Experience with DevSecOps, zero-trust networking, and security compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001. 
 - Previous experience in identity management, IAM, directory services, or security-focused SaaS environments. 
 - Contributions to open-source projects, technical publications, engineering blogs, or conference presentations focused on cloud platforms, infrastructure, or reliability engineering. 

Benefits

- Fully remote working arrangement, with the flexibility to work from anywhere within India. 
 - Opportunity to work on a globally distributed, AI-powered SaaS platform supporting modern IT infrastructure and security. 
 - High-impact technical ownership, with the opportunity to define cloud architecture and influence platform engineering strategy. 
 - Exposure to advanced cloud technologies, large-scale distributed systems, Kubernetes, and multi-region infrastructure. 
 - Opportunity to build and improve internal developer platforms that empower engineering teams to deliver products more efficiently. 
 - Access to AI-assisted development tools and opportunities to integrate emerging technologies into everyday engineering practices. 
 - Collaboration with experienced engineers and technical leaders across international teams. 
 - Opportunities to mentor senior engineering professionals and contribute to organization-wide technical standards.

 - Inclusive and collaborative remote-first working environment that values innovation, strong professional relationships, and continuous improvement.

data.title: AI Evals Engineer [SDET]
data.description:
About the Role: 

We are looking for a hands-on AI Evals Engineer to own how we measure, validate, and continuously improve the quality of our NLP, ML, Generative AI, and Agentic AI capabilities. You will design and build evaluation frameworks, datasets, and automated quality gates that give engineering and product teams real confidence before and after every release. This is a deeply technical, build-first role. You will write code every day: eval harnesses, LLM-as-judge pipelines, test datasets, and CI/CD integrations. A background in test automation and quality engineering, combined with strong AI fundamentals, is the ideal profile. 

What 'll be Responsible for?

- Design and build end-to-end evaluation frameworks for LLM-powered features, RAG pipelines, copilots, and multi-step agents. 
 - Create and curate high-quality evaluation datasets: golden sets, adversarial and edge-case sets, synthetic data, and production-derived regression sets, with clear versioning and labeling guidelines. 
 - Define task-specific quality metrics and rubrics covering accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, relevance, safety, toxicity, bias, latency, and cost. 
 - Build and calibrate LLM-as-judge pipelines, and validate them against human annotation (agreement, bias, and drift analysis). 
 - Evaluate agentic systems: tool-use correctness, planning and reasoning quality, trajectory analysis, task completion, error recovery, and guardrail adherence. 
 - Run red-teaming and robustness testing: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, and adversarial inputs. 
 - Integrate evals into CI/CD as automated quality gates, with regression detection across model, prompt, and retrieval changes. 
 - Set up online and offline monitoring for production quality: sampling, drift detection, feedback loops, and alerting. 
 - Partner with ML engineers, product managers, and developers to translate product requirements into measurable, testable quality criteria. 
 - Analyze failures, perform root-cause analysis, and turn findings into actionable recommendations for models, prompts, and system design. 
 - Mentor SQE1 and SQE2 engineers, and contribute to evaluation standards, best practices, and reusable internal tooling. 

What We'll look in you?

Technical Skills (Must-Have)

- 6 to 10 years of experience in software quality engineering, test automation, or SDET roles, with at least 1 to 2 years on AI/ML or LLM-based products. 
 - Strong hands-on programming in Python; working knowledge of one more language such as Java, TypeScript, or Go is a plus. 
 - NLP: tokenization, embeddings, semantic similarity, text classification, summarization, and NER; classical metrics such as BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and their limitations. 
 - Machine Learning: supervised and unsupervised learning, train/validation/test methodology, overfitting, data leakage, and metrics such as precision, recall, F1, AUC, and calibration. 
 - Generative AI: transformer and LLM concepts, prompting techniques, fine-tuning vs. RAG, context windows, sampling parameters, hallucination, and non-determinism. 
 - Agentic AI: agent architectures, tool/function calling, planning and memory, multi-agent orchestration, and protocols such as MCP. 
 - Practical experience designing evals for LLM applications: datasets, rubrics, LLM-as-judge, pairwise comparison, and human-in-the-loop review. 
 - Strong test automation foundations: framework design, API and service testing, CI/CD integration (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar), and test data management. 
 - Working knowledge of statistics for evals: sampling, confidence intervals, significance testing, inter-annotator agreement, and handling non-deterministic outputs. 
 - Preferred Skills (Good-to-Have)

- Hands-on experience with eval and observability tools such as Promptfoo, DeepEval, Ragas, LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, TruLens, OpenAI Evals. . 
 - Experience with LLM and agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, or the Claude and OpenAI SDKs. 
 - Familiarity with vector databases and retrieval evaluation (recall@k, MRR, nDCG, context precision and recall). 
 - Experience with AI safety and security testing: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, red-teaming, and guardrail validation. 
 - Exposure to MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model registries, data versioning, and production monitoring. 
 - Experience with performance, load, and cost testing of LLM-backed services. 
 - Background in Playwright, Selenium, Appium, REST Assured, pytest, or similar automation stacks. 
 - Cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) experience. 
 - Domain exposure to telecom, messaging, or CPaaS platforms is an added advantage. Behavioral Competencies

- Strong analytical thinking; turns ambiguous quality problems into clear, measurable engineering solutions. 
 - High ownership and ability to work independently while driving cross-team alignment. 
 - Excellent written and verbal communication; explains eval results and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 - Curiosity and a bias for learning in a fast-moving AI landscape. 

Why join us?

- Impactful Work: Play a key role in strengthening HR operations and delivering a seamless employee experience across the organisation. 
 - Tremendous Growth Opportunities: Be part of a rapidly growing company with opportunities to build and improve HR processes and practices. 
 - Innovative Environment: Work alongside a collaborative team in a dynamic environment where ownership, accountability and innovation are valued. Tanla is an equal opportunity employer. We champion diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

data.title: Supervisor, SAM & CLH
data.description:
Role Overview

The Software Asset & CLH Analyst III is the shift lead and technical anchor for one of the three IST-anchored shifts. The role carries two things at once: operational command of the shift - queue ownership, escalation resolution, and the handover into the next window - and the deepest technical expertise on the team, covering Corporate License Hosting server operations and the high-risk legal and contractual gating that junior levels are not authorised to clear. 

On the CLH side the analyst monitors the health of the global floating-licence servers, raises and validates licence file changes when contracts renew or quantities change, reads concurrent-usage metrics from the Altair Floating License Monitor, and works daemon drops to resolution inside the 4-hour SLA. On the governance side the analyst handles EULA and clickwrap reviews, checks the master review register before re-reviewing, routes signed agreements out of the standard queue and into formal legal cases, and supports publisher relationships and business reviews. Three of these roles exist, one per shift, and each is the senior decision-maker on duty when the manager is off the clock. 

CORE COMPETENCIES & EXPERTISE

To maintain operational excellence, analysts must demonstrate proficiency in the following key domains: 

- Foundational Licensing Knowledge: Deep understanding of perpetual, subscription, SaaS, and true-up models, including their unique compliance implications and operational requirements. 
 - Corporate License Hosting (CLH) Expertise: Advanced capability in managing floating-license servers, editing configuration files, working daemon drops within SLAs, and analyzing concurrent usage metrics via the Altair Floating License Monitor. 
 - Governance & Risk Management: Authority to manage high-risk EULA/clickwrap reviews, check master review registers, and enforce the prohibition on signed agreements within standard queues by routing them to formal legal channels. 
 - Compliance & Audit Proficiency: Mastery in constructing Initial and Final License Positions (ELP) by reconciling entitlement against usage evidence, and supporting publisher business reviews. 

Key Responsibilities

- Shift Leadership & Escalation Ownership
 - Own the shift: allocate work across the Level III, Level II and Level I analysts on duty, hold turnaround targets, and act as the senior decision-maker on the floor. 
 - Take and resolve escalations - customer complaints, blocked provisioning, entitlement disputes and licence failures - and judge correctly what must go to the ESAM Manager or the client rather than be absorbed. 
 - Run a clean handover into the next shift: open escalations, at-risk items and in-flight approvals documented and explicitly accepted, so nothing stalls in the gap. 
 - Mentor Level II analysts, review their complex casework, and build the bench for shift-lead cover. 
 - Monitor the portal and ticket queues for the shift, keeping ticket hygiene and category coding correct so reporting downstream is trustworthy. 
 - Corporate License Hosting (CLH) Server Operations
 - Monitor the health of the global licence servers hosting concurrent and floating licences, working daemon drops and service failures to resolution within the 4-hour critical SLA. 
 - Raise and validate 'Licence File Change' requests on contract renewal, quantity change or expiry, editing the flat text configuration files on the hosting servers correctly and reversibly. 
 - Read concurrent checkout and peak-usage metrics from the Altair Floating License Monitor - logging in strictly as a guest, and never entering corporate credentials without explicit system-administrator approval. 
 - Assess new hosting requests against the CLH eligibility criteria: native floating/concurrent licence support, Windows or Linux server compatibility, a supported server daemon (FlexNet preferred, others subject to compatibility review), no geolocation or policy usage restrictions, and an active informative catalogue item for user instructions. 
 - Apply the CLH request-routing matrix on unlisted floating-licence requests - checking the hosted-titles list, brokering spare capacity with the product champion and support owner on publicly shared pools, bypassing pool sharing on private pools, and capturing destination MAC addresses where a requester declines server hosting. 
 - Manage decommissioning: raise the support request to retire the daemon and remove licence files from the server when a hosted product is withdrawn. 
 - High-Risk Legal, EULA & Contract Gating
 - Own high-risk EULA and clickwrap review on the shift - copying non-signed agreements to secure storage and checking the master reviews register to confirm whether an approved review already exists within the last three years before triggering a new one. 
 - Enforce the signed-agreement prohibition: signed agreements are never accepted through the standard unlisted queue and must be routed via the contract intake path to be managed as formal legal cases. 
 - Identify and reject out-of-scope use cases on sight - code to be incorporated into customer-facing products, personal devices, and reverse engineering - using the standard responses and correct onward routing. 
 - Coordinate vendor security assessments and legal-review pipelines, and track the cases needing director-level signature through to execution by the client's signatory. The team never signs. 
 - Support the renewal milestone schedule as the technical owner of licence position - building the Initial and Final Licence Positions from usage scans and consumption snapshots. 
 - Publisher Governance, Audits & Continuous Improvement
 - Support publisher relationships and coordinate Semi-Annual Business Review inputs - performance data, utilisation evidence and action tracking - for the publishers in scope. 
 - Run the shift's weekly and monthly licence audits, and own the accuracy of savings and cost-avoidance entries in the licence-reclaim audit table. 
 - Identify automation candidates and author Business Requirements Documents where a publisher crosses 1, 000 transactions a year, moving work onto robotic process automation or vendor APIs. 
 - Own the technical escalation path into publishers and resellers for entitlement, key and activation failures the shift cannot resolve. 
 - Maintain and improve SOPs for the technical procedures on the shift, so CLH work is repeatable rather than resident in one person's head. 

PERFORMANCE & SERVICE LEVELS

Indicative performance targets for the role; final service levels are confirmed on engagement and measured per shift. 

- CLH Critical Response: resolve or contain critical Corporate License Hosting issues - daemon drops, server unavailability, checkout failures - within the 4-hour SLA. 
 - Shift SLA Attainment: hold the shift's queues to the committed targets, with listed software inside 3 days and standard SaaS provisioning inside 1 day. 
 - Escalation Resolution: own every escalation raised on the shift to closure or explicit handover, with no silent ageing. 
 - Handover Completeness: 100% of shifts closed with a documented, accepted handover. 
 - Legal & Authority Compliance: zero signed agreements processed through the unlisted queue; zero agreements signed by the team; 100% register check before a new legal review is raised. 
 - Licence Position Accuracy: Initial and Final Licence Positions delivered on the milestone dates and reconcilable to usage evidence. 
 - Audit & Savings Integrity: weekly and monthly audits completed, with reclamation entries complete and accurate enough to stand as the savings record. 

TOOLS & SYSTEMS

- CLH & Licence Servers: global floating-licence servers, FlexNet and other supported daemons, flat text licence configuration files, and the Altair Floating License Monitor. 
 - Entitlement & Usage: Flexera / ServiceNow SAM for entitlement and consumption tracking, plus usage scans and SaaS consumption snapshots for licence-position work. 
 - Contract & Legal: Deal Radar for contract and event records, and Pactfinder / Accord for legal review pipelines, NDA requests and signature validation. 
 - Queue & Automation: GUTS and Buganizer for ticket and bug management with strict category coding, and gHive / UiPath for automated reclamation. 
 - Financial: SAP Materials Management for purchase orders, amendments and three-way matching. 

Required Skills & Experience

Mandatory

- 6-10+ years in software asset management or software licensing operations, including experience as a shift lead, team lead or senior technical escalation point. 
 - Hands-on Corporate License Hosting or floating-licence server experience: FlexNet or comparable daemons, editing licence configuration files, troubleshooting daemon and service drops, and reading concurrent-usage metrics. 
 - Strong command of EULA and clickwrap review, licence terms and the commercial and legal risk they carry, with the judgment to stop a request rather than pass it through. 
 - Proven licence-position work - reconciling entitlement against deployed and consumed usage and defending the result. 
 - Comfortable working a rotating or fixed non-standard shift, including the NAMER window (22: 00-06: 00 IST). 
 - Clear English communication and the confidence to hold a technical or compliance line with client stakeholders and publishers. 

Preferred

- Software asset management certification (IAITAM CSAM, ITIL, Flexera or ServiceNow SAM credential). 
 - Linux and Windows server administration exposure sufficient to work licence-server issues with infrastructure teams. 
 - Scripting or automation literacy (Apps Script, Python, UiPath) for reclamation and reporting work. 
 - M&A software integration exposure, including termination workflows under privacy constraints. 
 - Experience supporting publisher business reviews and audit responses.

data.title: Principal Platform Software Engineer
data.description:
Job Description

Owns moderately complex components within platform services or SDKs; leads team-level improvements to integration frameworks and developer tooling. Performs deep debugging across a bounded set of distributed services, driving fixes that protect downstream consumers and upgrade paths. Analyzes usage, performance, and error budgets for specific platform surfaces; implements targeted resilience and capacity optimizations. Authors and curates team-scoped documentation, samples, and adoption guidance. 

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Platform Software Development: 

- Own a bounded platform component (service module, SDK area) and evolve its contracts for multi-tenant use. 
 - Perform deep debugging across a limited-service graph; drive compatibility-safe remediation plans. 
 - Implement targeted resilience/capacity patterns and document adoption guidance for team consumers. 

Software Development and Coding - Design, Testing, and Optimization: 

- Designs software solutions and analyzes and helps identify requirements to achieve business and operational goals, independently. 
 - Adheres to and suggests improvements to all phases of the software development lifecycle. 
 - Utilizes working knowledge to develop new software features and enhancements following design specifications and develops documents to clarify software design and code. 
 - Leads code reviews in designated areas to help drive improvements. 
 - Conducts debugging and troubleshooting to identify and fix moderately complex software issues. Develops fixes for identified issues. 
 - Implements software testing (e. g. , functional and non-functional testing), quality assurance processes, software error logging, monitoring, and observability for effective debugging, ensuring review by manager and/or lead throughout the process. 
 - Exercises judgment and discretion to conduct performance profiling and optimization of coding. 
 - Troubleshoots and resolves moderately complex issues related to application programming interface (API) functionality and integration. 
 - Implements moderately complex API versioning, lifecycle, and interoperability strategies. 

Software Architecture - Software System Structural Design: 

- Designs and develops software, systems, and services aligned to pre-defined system architecture. 
 - Develops working knowledge of software architecture decisions and best practices. 
 - Collaborates with team leads to review work to ensure alignment with software architecture. 
 - Implements moderately complex performance optimization and scalability strategies in software design. 

Issue/Defect Collaboration - Software Products Support: 

- Collaborates within and beyond immediate team to understand customer issues and align solutions. 
 - May provide technical guidance and support to customers regarding customer-reported issues, independently. 
 - Coaches, mentors, and guides others to advocate for customers' interests and suggests product enhancements based on feedback. 
 - Influences team to ensure customer satisfaction through timely resolution of issues and effective communication. 
 - Implements customer issue and/or defect handling and training processes, independently. 
 - Investigates and troubleshoots complex product maintenance issues to ensure customer agreement on short- and long-term solutions (e. g. , future enhancements). 

Practices and Standards Compliance - Security and Compliance: 

- Collaborates with the team to establish and follow development practices and coding standards. 
 - Exercises judgment and discretion to ensure code quality and adherence to broad acceptance criteria during development. 
 - Keeps up to date with industry best practices and applies them to software development processes. 
 - Implements secure coding practices to prevent security vulnerabilities. 

Development Operations - System Maintenance: 

- Performs periodic maintenance and testing operations for systems that require upgrading or patching (e. g. , for critical vulnerabilities). 
 - Exercises judgment and discretion to drive improvements, ensure automation, testing, and debugging of systems to ensure service/product availability, health, support, and reliability. 

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution: 

- Independently manages work, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure projects or initiatives stay on track and meet requirements. Proactively prioritizes work and adapts to resource or timeline shifts, suggesting adjustments to maintain project efficiency. 

Collaboration & Partnership: 

- Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others. 

Problem Solving: 

- Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices. 

Continuous Learning: 

- Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members. 

Continuous Improvement: 

- Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work.

Only Oracle brings together the data, infrastructure, applications, and expertise to power everything from industry innovations to life-saving care. And with AI embedded across our products and services, we help customers turn that promise into a better future for all. Discover your potential at a company leading the way in AI and cloud solutions that impact billions of lives.

Job Description

As a Test Automation Engineer, you will design and implement automation solutions that validate system behavior across UI, APIs, and integrations. You will contribute to building a robust quality engineering ecosystem by integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and supporting continuous delivery. 

In this role, you will translate requirements into effective test strategies, combining automation with manual, exploratory, and integration testing to ensure comprehensive quality coverage across all application layers. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys hands-on coding, solving complex validation challenges, and improving system quality at scale, while taking ownership of end-to-end quality outcomes and collaborating closely with cross-functional teams. 

Responsibilities

Automation Development & Framework Ownership

- Design, develop, and own scalable test automation frameworks and reusable components
 - Build automated test suites across: 
 - UI (Web/Mobile)
 - API and integration layers
 - Ensure automation solutions are maintainable, reliable, and extensible across teams

Test Strategy & Implementation

- Translate requirements into automation-ready test scenarios, test data, and validation strategies
 - Contribute to test strategy, coverage planning, and quality goals
 - Identify test gaps and proactively mitigate risks
 - Perform automation feasibility analysis to determine optimal test approach (manual vs automated)

Delivery & Execution Excellence

- Execute a balanced mix of automated and manual tests aligned with sprint goals, ensuring comprehensive validation across functional, integration, and edge-case scenarios. 
 - Contribute to task breakdown, estimation, and sprint commitments
 - Proactively raise risks, blockers, and testability concerns
 - Identify, log, prioritize, and track defects through resolution lifecycle
 - Perform root cause analysis and collaborate with development teams for fixes

Manual & Functional Testing

- Design, document, and execute detailed test cases and test scenarios
 - Perform functional, exploratory, and regression testing across features
 - Validate end-to-end workflows and business scenarios
 - Identify edge cases and usability issues through exploratory testing
 - Ensure test coverage for areas not suitable for automation

Quality, Standards & Engineering Practices

- Write clean, testable, and maintainable automation code
 - Participate in code reviews and continuous improvement of automation frameworks
 - Ensure adherence to Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD)
 - Take ownership of end-to-end quality outcomes across assigned areas
 - Follow established DevOps, security, and quality engineering practices

CI/CD & DevOps Integration

- Integrate automation into CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps preferred)
 - Enable continuous testing and shift-left quality practices
 - Monitor and improve pipeline stability, execution time, and reliability
 - Validate and troubleshoot system integrations, data flows, and error handling based on defined architectural designs and interfaces

Non-Functional Testing

- Contribute to performance, reliability, and resilience testing
 - Validate system behavior under load, stress, and failure scenarios

Observability & Debuggability

- Leverage logs, metrics, and traces to improve test reliability
 - Support root cause analysis of failures and improve system observability

Test Data & Environment Management

- Design and manage test data strategies and datasets
 - Ensure availability of stable, production-like test environments

Incident & Operational Support

- Assist in troubleshooting defects across environments
 - Support maintenance and continuous improvement of automation suites
 - Analyze and reduce flaky tests and unstable scenarios

Collaboration & Growth

- Collaborate with developers, QA, Product Owners, and Tech Leads
 - Actively learn and adopt new tools, frameworks, and best practices
 - Contribute to team knowledge sharing and a strong quality culture

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or related field
 - 5+ years of experience in software testing with strong automation focus
 - Experience in designing and implementing test automation frameworks
 - Strong understanding of testing principles, SDLC, STLC, and Agile practices

Technical Skills

- Programming experience in one or more: C#, Java, Python, JavaScript, Swift
 - Experience with automation tools such as Selenium, Katalon, Playwright, Cypress
 - Experience with: 
 - API testing (REST, Postman, etc. )

data.title: Lead MTS Verification Engineering
data.description:
Overview

Rambus, a premier chip and silicon IP provider making data faster and safer, is seeking to hire an exceptional Lead Verification Engineer to join our Security IP team in Bangalore In this role, you will be working with some of the brightest inventors and engineers in the world developing products that make data faster and safer. 

As a Lead Verification Engineer, you'll play a pivotal role in the verification of secure ASIC cores developed by Rambus Security Division (RSD), working with cross-functional teams including ASIC design engineers and architects, other verification engineers and system test engineers, security experts, and cryptographers. Cryptography and hardware security experience is not required, but an ability to, and interest in, learning about these areas is important In this full/-time role, you'll report directly to our Sr Manager Verification Engineering. 

Rambus offers a flexible work environment, embracing a hybrid approach for most office-based roles. Employees are encouraged to spend an average of at least three days per week onsite, allowing for two days of remote work. 

Responsibilities

- Lead the design and implementation of verification methodologies, test plans, testbenches, infrastructure, and platforms to produce thoroughly verified and robust products 
 - Partner closely with our architecture and design teams in specification and customer requirement reviews 
 - Represent verification methodologies in front of key customers and executive management 
 - Architect and help implement best verification practices, IP development and productization, quality assurance, release automation and improvements on the existing methodologies and flows 
 - Tackle sophisticated problems and develop scalable solutions that work across platforms 
 - Assist with all hardware project phases - bring-up, testing, debug, coverage analysis, and tracking 
 - Help with IP integration in partner environments and provide debug assistance to customer support teams

Qualifications

- BS or MS degree in electrical or computer engineering or closely related degree strongly preferred; but substantial, relevant, outstanding work experience may substitute in some cases 
 - Eight to Ten years of experience working as a verification engineer or related field 
 - Strong written and verbal communication skills: ability to explain complex concepts in front of technical audience 
 - Strong desire to take ownership of all verification aspects of a project, including team and methodology leadership 
 - Exposure to block-level and/or system-level verification 
 - Highly technical competence that includes a track record of effective verification of complex digital designs 
 - Solid understanding of standard ASIC verification techniques, including: 
 - Test planning 
 - Testbench creation 
 - Code and functional coverage 
 - Directed and SystemVerilog-based constrained random stimulus generation 
 - Self-checking - scoreboards, predictors, or reference models 
 - Assertions 
 - Solid understanding of verification methodologies (UVM or OVM) and standard testbench languages 
 - Comfortable with Unix development environments (make, scripting, SVN, etc. ), and with industry-standard EDA tools (VCS, Xcelium) 
 - Ability to support testbench lint/rule checking, profiling and automation using perl or python scripting 
 - Familiarity with advanced verification techniques such as object-oriented testbenches, fault/stimulus injection, FPGA prototyping and/or formal verification 
 - Protocol Knowledge 
 - APB, AXI and AXI Stream 
 - Ethernet/MACSec and IPSec 
 - Crypto-Algorithm AES, SM4 . . etc 
 Experience leading multi-site teams and projects, including task and schedule estimation

Beneficial Experience

- Experience in a customer-facing role 
 - Experience developing object-oriented testbench infrastructure in UVM 
 - Familiarity with IP integration, IP core delivery, and handoff issues 
 - Data, software, and/or network security; cryptography 
 - Ability to work with technical writers in the production of technical documentation

Personal Attributes

- Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills 
 - Able to communicate ideas in both technical and user-friendly language 
 - Able and willing to work in a team-oriented, collaborative environment 
 - Able to coordinate with internal and external teams across time zones 
 - A demonstrated ability to prioritize and execute tasks so as to achieve goals in an innovative, fast-paced, and often high-pressure environment 
 - Proven analytical and creative problem-solving abilities 
 - Passion for writing clean and neat code that adheres to coding standards

About Rambus

Rambus is a global company that makes industry-leading memory interface chips and Silicon IP to advance data center connectivity and solve the bottleneck between memory and processing. With over 30 years of semiconductor experience, we are a leading provider of high-performance products and innovations that maximize the bandwidth, capacity and security for AI and other data-intensive workloads. Our world-class team is the foundation of our company, and our innovative spirit drives us to develop the cutting-edge products and technologies essential for tomorrow's systems. 

s

Rambus is committed to cultivating a culture where we actively seek to understand, respect, and celebrate the complex and rich identities of ourselves and others. Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiatives are geared towards valuing the differences in backgrounds, experiences, and thoughts at Rambus to help enhance collaboration, teamwork, engagement, and innovation. At Rambus, we believe that we can be our best when every member of our organization feels respected, included, and heard. 

Rambus is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. 

Rambus is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans during our job application procedures. If you require assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please feel free to inform us in your application.

For more information about Rambus, visit rambus. com. For additional information on life at Rambus and our current openings, check out rambus. com/careers/ .

Role Overview

We are seeking a thorough SOC Physical Verification & Integration Specialist to drive the physical assembly and signoff of our next-generation SOCs. In this role, you will own the physical integration strategy from the floorplan stage through to tapeout, ensuring seamless assembly of massive multi-hierarchical blocks. You will act as the critical bridge between block-level implementation, top-level integration, and final foundry signoff, ensuring that complex physical bottlenecks are resolved without compromising power, performance, or area (PPA). 

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

- Top-Level Physical Integration: Drive the full-chip physical assembly of very large-scale SOCs (e. g. , multi-billion transistor designs). Manage top-level floorplanning, bump planning, global power grid (PG) integration, and top-level clock/routing integration. 
 - Hierarchical Verification Methodology: Architect and deploy highly efficient, hierarchical physical verification (PV) flows. Define the boundary conditions, abstraction models, and interface rules required to assemble heavily partitioned, massive-scale designs. 
 - Signoff Execution & Debugging: Own full-chip DRC, LVS, ERC, Antenna, ESD, and Latch-up signoff using industry-standard tools (e. g. , Siemens Calibre) at advanced process nodes (5nm, 3nm, or below). 
 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner tightly with the Physical Design (PD) and Static Timing Analysis (STA) teams. Proactively resolve integration conflicts-such as top-level routing congestion or interface timing violations-ensuring that physical fixes do not disrupt timing closure. 
 - Design Rule Co-Optimization: Work directly with foundry partners to interpret complex design rules and waive or resolve edge-case violations specific to reticle-limit designs. 
 - Automation & Flow Development: Develop robust scripts and utilities to automate physical integration tasks, database merging, and PV result parsing to accelerate the tapeout cycle. 

Qualifications

- Experience: 14-20 Years
 - Technology Focus: Sub-5nm (3nm/2nm)
 - Required Qualifications
 - Experience: 14-20 + years of hands-on experience in SOC physical design and physical verification, with a proven track record of taping out very large, complex SOCs (e. g. , Datacenter, AI accelerators, or High-Performance Compute chips). 
 - Technical Domain Expertise: * Deep understanding of the entire RTL-to-GDSII flow, with expert-level knowledge of physical integration challenges in flat vs. hierarchical methodologies. 
 - Strong foundational understanding of Physical Design and Static Timing Analysis (STA) to effectively communicate with implementation teams and assess the timing impact of PV fixes. 
 - Tool Proficiency: * Mastery of top-level integration tools (Cadence Innovus). 
 - Expertise in physical verification suites (e. g. , Siemens Calibre nmDRC/nLVS/PERC, Synopsys IC Validator). 
 - Familiarity with chip/package co-design and bump planning tools. 
 - Programming/Scripting: High proficiency in Tcl, Python, and/or Perl for EDA flow automation and database manipulation. 
 - Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
